Heaven they must inherit. Now herein is a high degree of salvation, and a great part of the purpose of Christ's coming: to bring his saints into Heaven. Thither he has gone before this to prepare the same for them, and now he shall come again to give them the possession thereof: "Come, enter into Heaven." Heaven! What is Heaven! Certainly it is not just a single particular palace, but a city, a capital city, a mother-city <note>original: *Moeder-stadt* - used here to signify the primary or original city from which others derive.</note>, the first City of God's creation. The angel, bringing John in the spirit <margin>Revelation 21:10, 11</margin> onto a great and high mountain, showed him the great City, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of Heaven from God, and having the glory of God. ### C O N C L U S I O N.

And now, my brothers, I have delivered my message, to which Christ has sent me; I believe completely that I—having now dealt with this work of the Eternal Gospel, or the carrying out by Christ of the great work of our salvation—have been somewhat long in speaking, but also how long in the doing! Let me give you a brief display of that which I have said, and of that which has been done from eternity, and shall be done unto eternity. Remember that God in His eternity took a design or purpose to glorify the riches of His grace in the saving of sinners; and to that end He first decreed a Christ. 2. Immediately after the fall, He promised the sealed Christ. 3. In the fullness of time, He gave the promised Christ; then that same Christ took on our nature, and united it with His Divinity into one person; and in that person He was born, lived, died, and rose again, and ascended into Heaven, and there He has now sat, sent down His Holy Spirit, and offered His holy prayers for over sixteen hundred years <note>This identifies the author as writing in the 17th century.</note>. And in this final work He shall persevere until the end of the world, and then He shall come again to judge the world, and to take His holy ones to Himself, so that they may be where He is, to see and enjoy Him for all eternity. This

<column-break/>

is the short summary of all that I have said; only in every part I have set forth Christ’s workings for us, and our workings for Christ; in various forms and outflows <note>original: "upt-vloepinghen," referring to the internal movements or emanations of the soul</note> of His love He has wrought for us, and in various forms and outflows of our souls we are taught how we must work properly and fittingly for Him.

But how does God’s free grace shine in all these dealings in Christ; <margin>Ephes. 2:5</margin> *By grace you are saved,* says the Apostle in Ephesians 2:5. <margin>Ephesians 2:5</margin> The decree, the means, and the end of our salvation is grace, and grace alone. The decree is grace, <margin>Romans 11:5</margin> and therefore it is called the election of grace; <margin>2 Timothy 1:9</margin> the means are of grace, and therefore we are called according to His grace; <margin>Romans 3:24</margin> and we are justified freely by His grace; <margin>Romans 6:23</margin> and the end is of grace, for eternal life is the gift of God’s grace; both the beginning, the progress, and the completion is all of grace; <margin>Ephesians 1:7; chapter 2</margin> this is the riches of His grace, the exceeding riches of His grace; the conclusion of everything is this: God's free grace having been first designed, shall finally be revealed, and eternally praised by the saints and the angels; that same free grace, which from the beginning of God’s age, from eternity has hovered over the blessed design and sweet purpose of our salvation, shall finally be properly glorified, when—

<meta>This page concludes the work, moving from the theological description of Christ’s supremacy to a direct, pastoral appeal to the reader to personally claim Christ’s work as their own.</meta>

# Looking unto Jesus.

...the first in the morning, and the last at night. Shall I speak just one more word to you who believe? Oh, take for yourself particularly <term>take for yourself|The Dutch 'toe-eygent' (to appropriate) refers to the act of taking the general promises of the Gospel and applying them to one's own soul</term> all the actions of Jesus Christ; remember how He came for you out of His Father’s bosom <note>original: "schoot", literally lap or womb, but traditionally translated as bosom in this context</note>, wept and bled for you; how He poured out His life for you; He has now risen for you, ascended into Heaven for you, sits at the right hand of God, and governs the whole

<column-break/>

world for you; He prays for you, and at the end of the world He shall come again for you, and take you to Himself, to live with Him for all eternity. Truly, if you believe and live in this way, your life will be full of comfort, and your death shall be sweet; if there is any Heaven on earth, you shall find it in the contemplation and practice of this Gospel-duty <note>the 'duty' refers to the spiritual discipline described throughout the book</note>, in looking unto Jesus.

## THE END.

<image-desc>A symmetrical ornamental tailpiece consisting of intricate scrolling foliage and floral motifs, tapering downwards to a decorative point.</image-desc>

<summary>The final passage of the book exhorts believers to personally appropriate Christ's sacrifice and heavenly reign, promising that the spiritual practice of "looking unto Jesus" brings a "Heaven on earth" and comfort in death.</summary>
<keywords>Jesus Christ, Gospel-duty, salvation, appropriation of faith, eternity, comfort, looking unto Jesus</keywords>
